findings.capture_cap_distinction: The proposed SOURCE payload 1MiB capture cap is reader storage, not a pipe-size guarantee. The separate local 128KiB cap applies to launcher receipt only.
findings.limits: No claim that every target schedule must fail. Actual target pipe capacity, delivery and final parent/payload integration are UNVERIFIED. This is a source liveness regression for an ordinary allowed pipe schedule, not a measured runtime failure.
findings.minimal_repair: For successful durable result publication, retain its exact reference and emit a separately closed compact success receipt within a justified one-write pipe allowance. Bind its semantics in parent handling and retain all full records, failure details, actual exits/EOF and original phase/caps. Do not grant success from a result file alone. Do not add a second writer, retry a partial summary, add time or change common/startup flags.
findings.normal_capacity_example: 65536 immediately writable bytes with no reader progress leaves at least143580 bytes unsent. This is an arithmetic/static pipe witness, not an observed target capacity or runtime result.
findings.static_path: emit_summary sets fd1 nonblocking, attempts the full result once, rejects a partial count, main returns1 and the entry block uses os._exit(1). The omitted tail is never sent. Parent then gets partial JSON and actual failure even though command/data work succeeded.
findings.title: Keep the normal full-result summary out of a single nonblocking pipe write
findings.trigger: All finite commands and the durable result succeed; normal bounded pipe stdout has less immediately writable space than the full encoded result, and its reader makes no progress during the nonblocking write.

prior_disposition.reason: Explicit integer clock6 domain and conservative local conversion remain AST-exact; no old absolute time is retagged; parent causal inspection remains external.

No caller-owned buffered source/stdout payload remains; explicit raw close has no Python payload to flush and is not retried; os._exit bypasses finalization. No new clearance of unchanged common cleanup or OS-stall behavior.
